text_blocks.snippet: The virus, known as varicella-zoster virus (VZV), can spread through direct contact with the fluid from the blisters of a person with shingles. People who have had chickenpox previously have the virus dormant in their bodies and are not at risk of getting shingles from someone with shingles.

However, if a person who has never had chickenpox comes into contact with the fluid from shingles blisters, they can develop chickenpox. This is why it is important for people with shingles to avoid contact with people who are not immune to chickenpox.
The shingles virus is most contagious when the blisters are open and weeping. Once the blisters have crusted over, the person is no longer contagious.
